summary: Untrusted templates are silently ignored by default; the experimental `_ANSIBLE_TEMPLAR_UNTRUSTED_TEMPLATE_BEHAVIOR` environment variable can be set to warning, error or ignore to troubleshoot.
questions: Why is my template not being rendered and just shown as-is?
How do I get warnings when Ansible skips an untrusted template?
How do I debug template trust issues in ansible-core 2.19?

answer_card.title: Troubleshoot untrusted templates
answer_card.answer_md:
By default, untrusted templates are **silently ignored** and used as-is. To troubleshoot, set the environment variable `_ANSIBLE_TEMPLAR_UNTRUSTED_TEMPLATE_BEHAVIOR`:

- `warning`: issue a warning when an untrusted template is encountered
- `error`: raise an error
- `ignore`: silently use the string as-is (the default)

This behavior is experimental and may change in future versions.
